name: Earth-fault current relay
summary: Measuring relay form that operates on current flowing to earth, fed from a residual connection or core-balance CT.
description: The earth-fault current relay form identifies a relay whose operating quantity is current flowing to earth. It may be fed from a core-balance CT around all live conductors, from the residual connection of three phase CTs, or from a CT in the star-point earth lead, and the source changes its achievable sensitivity.

The relay box shows the quantity with an earth qualifier but not the setting, characteristic or whether it is directional. In resistance-earthed and isolated networks earth-fault current is small and often needs a sensitive or directional element that must be stated separately.
readingNotes: Identify the CT arrangement that supplies the residual current.
Check whether the element is directional or sensitive.
distinction: An earth-fault current relay measures current to earth; an earth-fault voltage relay measures neutral displacement voltage.
